a2-01.q: Fill in the blanks: El sábado Ana ___ tarde a la estación y después ___ por el andén.
a2-01.why: Ana is 'she': -ar verbs take -ó (llegó) and -er verbs take -ió (corrió). Llegió and corró mix up the two endings; llegué and corrí are the 'I' forms.

a2-01.q: Which sentence correctly says 'Ana saw her phone and said hello'?
options: Ana vio su teléfono y dijo hola.
Ana vio su teléfono y dició hola.
Ana vió su teléfono y dijo hola.
Ana veyó su teléfono y dijo hola.
a2-01.why: Ver gives vio, with no written accent (like dio and fue). Decir has the irregular stem dij- and ends in plain -o: dijo, not dició.

a2-01.topic: Ir a + infinitive, and ir a + place
a2-01.q: What does 'Voy a llegar primero' mean, compared with 'Voy a Valencia'?
options: Both are future plans with a verb after 'a'.
Both mean that I already went somewhere.
The first is a destination; the second is a future plan.
The first is a future plan (I'm going to arrive first); the second is a destination (I'm going to Valencia).
a2-01.why: After a, an infinitive (llegar) signals a near-future plan, while a place (Valencia) tells you where you are going.

a2-01.topic: Reflexive verbs: se sentó, se casa
a2-01.q: What does 'Mi hermana se casa a las cinco' mean?
options: My sister goes home at five.
My sister got married at five.
My sister marries herself at five.
My sister is getting married at five.
a2-01.why: Casarse means 'to get married' (se is not 'herself' here), and the present tense can describe a scheduled event. 'Got married' would be se casó, and se casa has nothing to do with casa (house).

a2-01.q: Which sentence has a mistake in the preterite?
options: Ana y Pablo llegaron a Valencia.
a2-01.why: Subir is an -ir verb, so the 'they' form ends in -ieron: subieron. The -aron ending is only for -ar verbs (llegaron).

a2-01.q: Fill in the blank: Los padres de Ana ___ que el tren tenía una avería.
a2-01.why: After the j of the stem dij-, the 'they' ending is -eron, not -ieron: dijeron. Decir never uses a regular stem in the preterite, so decieron is wrong.

a2-01.topic: Ir a + infinitive, and ir a + place
a2-01.q: Fill in the blank: Mañana yo ___ tocar la guitarra en la boda.
a2-01.why: The near future is ir + a + infinitive: voy a tocar. 'Voy tocar' drops the a, va a is the wrong person, and al (a + el) only goes before a masculine noun: voy al pueblo.

a2-01.topic: Reflexive verbs: se sentó, se casa
a2-01.q: Fill in the blanks: —Hola, ___ llamo Pablo. ¿Y tú, cómo ___ llamas?
a2-01.why: The reflexive pronoun matches the subject: (yo) me llamo, (tú) te llamas, (él/ella) se llama.

a2-02.topic: Preterite of regular and irregular verbs
a2-02.q: Which sentence means 'Yesterday Sofía went to the market'?
a2-02.why: Ir has the irregular preterite fue (shared with ser), written without an accent; al mercado shows it means 'went'. Va is present, and fué and iró don't exist.

a2-02.q: The note in the box tells Sofía to go to the market. Which tú command completes it? 'Primero, ___ al mercado.'
a2-02.why: Ir has an irregular tú command: ve. Va and vas are present-tense statements ('goes', 'you go'), and ves comes from ver ('you see').

a2-02.topic: Object pronouns: le dio, te lo regala
a2-02.q: In 'Ella te lo regala', what does lo stand for, and why does te come first?
options: Lo is the thing given (the puppy); te is the person receiving, and the indirect pronoun always goes first.
Lo means 'to him', so it should really go before te.
Lo is the person receiving; te is the thing given.
Lo is the puppy, but the order is free, so 'lo te regala' is also correct.
a2-02.why: With two pronouns, the indirect one (to whom: te) goes first and the direct one (what: lo = el cachorro) second: te lo = it to you. 'Lo te' is never correct.

a2-02.q: Put the story events in order: 'Entonces, el perro saltó a sus brazos. Primero, Sofía abrió la caja. Después, corrió por la calle.'
options: Primero, Sofía abrió la caja. Después, corrió por la calle. Entonces, el perro saltó.
Después, corrió por la calle. Primero, abrió la caja. Entonces, el perro saltó.
Primero, el perro saltó. Entonces, abrió la caja. Después, corrió.
Entonces, el perro saltó. Después, corrió. Primero, abrió la caja.
a2-02.why: Primero starts the sequence, después (afterwards) continues it, and entonces (then, at that moment) introduces what happened next.

a2-02.topic: Preterite of regular and irregular verbs
a2-02.q: In 'Ayer fue el cumpleaños de Sofía', what does fue mean?
a2-02.why: Fue is the preterite of both ser and ir. Here nobody moves to a place; it describes the day, so it's ser: 'Yesterday was Sofía's birthday.'

a2-02.q: Turn the statement into a tú command for Sofía: 'Sofía lleva los mangos a la panadería' > '___ los mangos a la panadería, Sofía.'
a2-02.why: For regular verbs, the tú command looks like the he/she present: lleva. Llevas is a statement ('you take'), lleve is the formal usted command, and llevar is the infinitive.

a2-02.topic: Object pronouns: le dio, te lo regala
a2-02.q: Fill in the blank: Doña Lupe ___ dio una bolsa de mangos (a Sofía).
a2-02.why: Sofía receives the bag, so she is the indirect object: le = to her. La would make Sofía the thing given, and se is not used alone here.

a2-02.q: Fill in the blank: El abuelo llegó a las nueve ___ mañana.
a2-02.why: After a clock time, Spanish uses de la mañana (at nine in the morning). Without a clock time it's por la mañana: Por la mañana, el abuelo llegó.

a2-03.q: How do you say 'I took the bus' in the preterite?
a2-03.why: For yo, -ar verbs end in -é: tomé. Tomó is he/she, tomo (no accent) is the present 'I take', and -í is the yo ending for -er/-ir verbs.

a2-03.topic: Irregular preterite: fue, puso, hice, dijo
a2-03.q: Fill in the blank: Abuela, ayer yo ___ tu receta.
a2-03.why: Hacer has the irregular stem hic-, and the yo form ends in -e with no accent: hice. Hizo is he/she (c becomes z); hací and hicé don't exist.

a2-03.q: Mateo tastes the dish (el plato) he has just cooked. How does he say 'It tastes good'?
a2-03.why: Estar describes how food tastes as you experience it: está rico. Es rico would describe a general quality (and with a person, ser rico means 'to be rich'). Hay means 'there is'.
Lo (it) attaches to the infinitive: decirlo = to say it. 'Tell him' would be decirle, and puedo is present, so it isn't 'didn't'.

a2-03.q: What is the difference between 'cocino' and 'cocinó'?
options: Cocino = I cook (present); cocinó = he/she cooked (preterite).
Cocino = I cooked; cocinó = he/she cooks.
Cocino is used in Spain, cocinó in Latin America.
a2-03.why: The written accent moves the stress and changes the tense and person: cocino (I cook, present) vs cocinó (he/she cooked, preterite).

a2-03.topic: Irregular preterite: fue, puso, hice, dijo
options: Mateo puso aceite en la sartén.
a2-03.why: Irregular preterites never take a written accent: hizo, puso, dijo, fue. 'Hizó' is wrong.

a2-03.q: Fill in the blanks: —¿Dónde ___ la receta? —En el cuaderno. ___ una receta muy vieja.
a2-03.why: Location uses estar (¿Dónde está?), and saying what something is (identity) uses ser: Es una receta muy vieja.

a2-03.q: Fill in the blank: Para la receta, ___ dos ingredientes.
a2-03.why: Faltar works like gustar: the missing things are the subject, so the verb agrees with them. Dos ingredientes is plural, so faltan; falta is for one thing (falta algo).

a2-04.q: Which sentence describes a childhood habit?
options: Ayer jugó al fútbol en la calle.
Todos los días jugaba al fútbol en la calle.
Jugué una vez al fútbol en la calle.
Va a jugar al fútbol en la calle.
a2-04.why: The imperfect (jugaba) with todos los días describes a regular habit in the past. Jugó and jugué are single events, and va a jugar is the future.

a2-04.q: Fill in the blank: Esta vez yo ___ tirar a la derecha, pero mi pie decidió otra cosa.
a2-04.why: Querer has the irregular preterite stem quis-, and the yo form is quise, with no accent. Quiso is he/she, and querí doesn't exist.

a2-04.q: Fill in the blank: Faltaban dos minutos cuando el árbitro ___ un penalti.
a2-04.why: The referee's whistle is the event that interrupts the background (faltaban dos minutos), so it takes the preterite: pitó.

a2-04.q: How do you say 'Their grandmother was waiting for them'?
a2-04.why: Estar in the imperfect + gerund (-ando) gives an action in progress in the past, with the pronoun before estaba. Esperado is the participle, not the gerund.

a2-04.q: Fill in the blank: Cuando Tomás ___ niño, vivía en Medellín.
a2-04.why: Describing a stage of life (cuando era niño) is background, so it takes the imperfect of ser: era. Estar isn't used for 'being a child', and es is present.

a2-04.q: Camila asks Tomás: '¿Cómo lo supiste?' What does she mean?
options: How did you find out (know) it?
How did you use to know it?
a2-04.why: Supiste is the irregular preterite of saber (stem sup-). In the preterite, saber means 'found out' or 'knew' at that moment.

a2-04.q: Which sentence correctly says 'Tomás was very nervous, but he remembered something'?
options: Tomás estuvo muy nervioso, pero recordaba algo.
Tomás fue muy nervioso, pero recordó algo.
Tomás está muy nervioso, pero recordó algo.
Tomás estaba muy nervioso, pero recordó algo.
a2-04.why: His nervousness is the background (imperfect of estar: estaba), and remembering is the event (preterite: recordó). Ser is not used for a temporary feeling.

a2-04.q: Which is another correct way to say 'Su abuela los estaba esperando'?
a2-04.why: The pronoun can go before estaba or be attached to the gerund. When it's attached, add a written accent to keep the stress: esperándolos.

a2-05.q: Which sentence sets the scene (weather and time) at the start of a story?
options: Llovió mucho y fue de noche.
Llovía mucho y era de noche.
Va a llover y es de noche.
a2-05.why: Weather and time of day are background, so the imperfect is used: llovía, era. Llovió and fue present them as completed events.

a2-05.q: How do you say 'I was working' (at that moment)?
a2-05.why: Imperfect of estar + gerund (-ando) describes an action in progress at a past moment. Trabajado is the participle.

a2-05.q: Fill in the blank: De repente, su teléfono ___.
a2-05.why: De repente signals a sudden single event, so the preterite: sonó. Sonar is an -ar verb, so the ending is -ó (sonió is wrong).

a2-05.q: Which sentence means 'She put on her coat'?
a2-05.why: Ponerse + clothing = to put on (yourself): se puso el abrigo. Le puso el abrigo means she put the coat on someone else, and puso never takes an accent.

a2-05.q: Fill in the blank: Ella vivía en el número 7, y en la calle ___ un chico con una mochila roja.
a2-05.why: Había (the past of hay) introduces what existed in the scene: 'there was'. It stays singular even with plural nouns, era can't mean 'there was', and hay is present.

a2-05.q: What does 'La mamá de Nicolás bajó corriendo' mean?
options: Nicolás's mother used to run downstairs every day.
Nicolás's mother got out of the car in a hurry (running).
Nicolás's mother got out of the car and stopped running.
Nicolás's mother is going to run.
a2-05.why: A gerund after a movement verb says how the action was done: bajó corriendo = she got out running, in a hurry. Bajó is one preterite event, not a habit.

a2-05.q: What is the he/she preterite of leer?
a2-05.why: When an -er/-ir stem ends in a vowel, -ió becomes -yó: leer > leyó, oír > oyó, creer > creyó.

a2-05.q: Fill in the blank: Los dos ___ sentaron bajo el techo del porche.
a2-05.why: The reflexive pronoun matches the subject: los dos (they) > se sentaron. Nos would need nosotros (nos sentamos).

a2-06.q: Which sentence correctly says 'Camila liked the building'?
options: A Camila la gustaba el edificio.
A Camila le gustaba el edificio.
a2-06.why: Gustar works backwards: the building is what pleases, so the verb agrees with el edificio (singular), and le (indirect) marks Camila.

a2-06.q: How do you say 'Try it' (la bombilla) as a tú command?
a2-06.why: An affirmative command attaches the pronoun to the end, and a written accent keeps the stress on prue-: pruébala. La prueba means 'she tries it' (or 'the test').

a2-06.q: What does 'Camila se puso a llorar' mean?
options: Camila put herself on the floor.
Camila was crying all day, every day.
a2-06.why: Ponerse a + infinitive means to start doing something: se puso a llorar = she started crying.

a2-06.q: What does 'Vamos a subir todo por la escalera' express?
options: We went up the stairs yesterday.
We're going to carry everything up the stairs (or: let's carry it all up).
We always go up the stairs.
a2-06.why: Vamos a + infinitive describes what is going to happen and can also suggest 'let's'. It is not past and not a habit.

a2-06.q: Fill in the blank: A Camila le ___ mucho las ventanas enormes.
a2-06.why: With gustar the thing liked is the subject. Las ventanas is plural, so the verb is plural: le gustaban.
Di is the irregular tú command of decir; me (to me) and lo (it) attach to the end, indirect first: dímelo. 'Give it to me' would be dámelo.

a2-06.q: Fill in the blank: Camila ___ a un apartamento nuevo el sábado.
a2-06.why: Moving house is mudarse (reflexive): se mudó. Moverse means to move your body, and mudó without se doesn't mean 'moved house'.

options: Esta lámpara va a darte luz.
Esta lámpara te va a dar luz.
Tomás va a comprar una bombilla.
Esta lámpara va te a dar luz.
a2-06.why: With ir a + infinitive, the pronoun goes before the conjugated verb (te va a dar) or attaches to the infinitive (va a darte), never in the middle.

a2-07.q: Fill in the blank: Todas las tardes Mateo tocaba la guitarra, pero un jueves se ___ una cuerda.
a2-07.why: The routine is imperfect (tocaba), and the one-time event on a Thursday is preterite: se rompió.

a2-07.q: Mateo showed the guitar to Ernesto. Which is correct, replacing 'la guitarra' with a pronoun?
a2-07.why: Le becomes se before lo/la, the indirect pronoun comes first, and la is feminine to match la guitarra.

a2-07.q: Fill in the blank: Es muy bonita, pero es más vieja que ___.
a2-07.why: After que in a comparison, use the subject pronoun: más vieja que yo (older than me / than I am). Mí is only used after prepositions such as para (para mí).

a2-07.q: What is the tú command for 'Come with me'?
a2-07.why: Venir has a short irregular tú command: ven. Viene and vienes are statements, and 'vene' doesn't exist. (In Buenos Aires, with vos, you'll also hear vení.)

a2-07.q: Which time phrase goes with the imperfect in this story?
a2-07.why: Todas las tardes describes a routine, so it goes with the imperfect (tocaba). The others point to one moment and go with the preterite.

a2-07.q: In 'Ernesto le cambió la cuerda', who or what is le?
options: Mateo: Ernesto changed the string for him
a2-07.why: Le is an indirect pronoun: the person who benefits (for him = Mateo). The string is the direct object, la cuerda.

a2-07.q: Which sentence correctly says 'Julieta is his best student'?
options: Julieta es su más buena alumna.
Julieta es su alumna más mejor.
Julieta es mejor alumna que él.
a2-07.why: Bueno has the irregular form mejor; with a possessive it means 'best': su mejor alumna. 'Más buena' and 'más mejor' are wrong here.

a2-07.q: In 'Ahora Mateo toca en la plaza', is toca a command?
options: Yes, it tells Mateo to play.
Yes, it's a formal usted command.
No, it's present tense: 'Mateo plays in the square'.
a2-07.why: Toca can be a tú command or the he/she present. Here Mateo is the subject of a statement, so it's present tense. As a command: ¡Toca para nosotros!

a2-08.q: Fill in the blank: Jairo ___ delante cuando Andrés se paró.
a2-08.why: Jairo's walking is the ongoing background action (imperfect: caminaba), while se paró is the event that happens during it.

a2-08.q: Which is the correct tú command for 'Try it' (el chocolate)?
a2-08.why: The tú command is prueba (o > ue); add the pronoun to the end and write an accent: pruébalo. Probarlo is the infinitive.

a2-08.q: What does 'Solo se oía el viento' mean?
options: Only the wind could be heard.
a2-08.why: Here se doesn't mean 'itself': se + verb without a named person means 'could be heard', like an English passive.

a2-08.q: Which phrase correctly means 'the tallest palms in the world'?
options: más las palmas altas del mundo
las palmas más altas que el mundo
las palmas más altas del mundo
a2-08.why: The superlative is el/la/los/las + noun + más + adjective + de (not que, not 'en').

a2-08.q: Why does the story say 'Durante la mañana, el paisaje fue precioso' (preterite) instead of 'era'?
options: Because it sums up a closed period (that morning) as a whole.
Because the scenery is still beautiful now.
a2-08.why: The preterite can sum up a bounded period: durante la mañana marks a finished stretch of time. Era would describe the scenery as background. Fue here is from ser, not ir.

a2-08.q: Jairo tells Andrés (tú): 'If there's fog, follow the river.' Fill in: Si hay niebla, ___ el río.
a2-08.why: The tú command is the he/she present form, stem change included: seguir > sigue (e > i; the u keeps the hard g sound). Siguió is the preterite.

a2-08.q: Fill in the blank: Al mediodía, el cielo ___ gris.
a2-08.why: Ponerse + adjective = to become/turn (a change): el cielo se puso gris. Without se, poner means 'to put', and ponerse a needs an infinitive.

a2-08.q: Fill in the blank: Andrés estaba ___ asustado que no podía pensar.
a2-08.why: Tan + adjective + que = so ... that. Tanto goes with nouns or verbs (tanto miedo), muy can't be followed by que, and más ... que would be a comparison.

a2-09.q: Fill in the blank: Mientras ella ___ el metro, un señor chocó con ella.
a2-09.why: Mientras introduces the ongoing background action (imperfect: esperaba), and chocó is the event that interrupts it.

a2-09.q: How do you say 'I have never been late'?
a2-09.why: Present perfect = he + participle (-ado for -ar verbs): he llegado. Nunca goes before he, and nothing goes between he and the participle. Llegando is the gerund.

a2-09.q: What does 'Se me cayó un café' mean?
options: I dropped the coffee on purpose.
I fell down in a café.
I dropped a coffee by accident.
a2-09.why: Se + me + verb presents an unplanned event: the coffee is the subject (cayó agrees with café) and me shows who it happened to. 'I fell' would be me caí.

a2-09.q: Mrs. Ortega says to Daniela in the interview: 'Llega tarde.' What does the verb form show?
options: It is a command to arrive.
Tú is used (informal); llega is the tú form.
Usted is used (formal), with the he/she verb form.
a2-09.why: Formal usted takes the he/she verb form (llega, tiene). With tú it would be llegas, tienes.

a2-09.q: Why is repasaba in the imperfect in 'Mientras esperaba el metro, repasaba sus respuestas'?
options: It is an ongoing action, happening at the same time as esperaba.
It is a completed single event.
It happened after she got on the subway.
It is something she did every day for years.
a2-09.why: Two actions in progress at the same time in the past both take the imperfect: mientras esperaba..., repasaba... (she was going over her answers).

a2-09.q: Fill in the blank: ¿Has ___ antes con clientes?
a2-09.why: Present perfect = haber + participle (-ado/-ido). The participle doesn't change for gender (not trabajada), and trabajando is the gerund.

a2-09.q: Fill in the blank: Se me ___ las llaves. (I dropped my keys.)
a2-09.why: In the accidental se structure, the verb agrees with the thing that fell: las llaves (plural) > cayeron. Me shows who it happened to.

a2-09.q: The older woman asks with tú: '¿Sabes dónde está la oficina?' How would she ask with usted?
a2-09.why: Usted uses the he/she form: (usted) sabe. Sabes is the tú form, and sabéis is vosotros (plural, Spain).

a2-10.q: Fill in the blanks: Cada año, todos los vecinos ___ faroles, pero ese viernes ___ a llover.
a2-10.why: Cada año marks a habit (imperfect: hacían), and ese viernes marks a single event (preterite: empezó). Hacieron is not a real form; the preterite is hicieron.

a2-10.q: Which sentence means 'It's the biggest lantern in the village'?
options: Es el farol más grande del pueblo.
Es farol el más grande en pueblo.
Es el farol más grande que el pueblo.
Es el farol grande más del pueblo.
a2-10.why: The superlative is el + noun + más + adjective + de (del = de + el), where English uses 'in'.

a2-10.topic: Object pronouns: se lo, le, la
a2-10.q: Pablo told the neighbors the news (la noticia). Which is correct with pronouns?
options: Pablo se la contó a los vecinos.
Pablo le la contó a los vecinos.
Pablo les la contó a los vecinos.
Pablo la les contó a los vecinos.
a2-10.why: Le/les changes to se before lo/la/los/las, the indirect pronoun comes first, and la matches la noticia.

a2-10.topic: Perfect tenses: he visto, había aprendido
a2-10.q: Fill in the blank: Cuando Inés llegó al granero, la lluvia ya ___ el papel.
a2-10.why: The rain soaked the paper before another past moment (when Inés arrived), so use the past perfect: había + participle. Ha mojado connects to now, not to a past moment.

a2-10.q: Why is viajaba in the imperfect in 'Cada agosto, Inés viajaba al pueblo de su abuelo'?
options: Viajar is irregular in the preterite.
It describes a repeated habit (every August).
a2-10.why: Cada agosto signals something that happened regularly, so the imperfect is used. A single trip would be viajó.

a2-10.q: Fill in the blanks: Después de la lluvia, el toro era ___ bonito ___ antes.
a2-10.why: To compare two things: más + adjective + que. Más de is used before numbers (más de cien personas), and tan pairs with como.

a2-10.topic: Object pronouns: se lo, le, la
a2-10.q: What does 'Su abuelo le tomó la mano' mean?
options: Her grandfather took his own hand.
Her grandfather shook hands with everyone.
Her grandfather gave her his hand.
a2-10.why: With body parts Spanish uses the article (la mano) and shows whose it is with the indirect pronoun le (her), not with a possessive.

a2-10.topic: Perfect tenses: he visto, había aprendido
options: Nunca he veído trabajar tan rápido a este pueblo.
Nunca he visto trabajar tan rápido a este pueblo.
Nunca visto he trabajar tan rápido a este pueblo.
Nunca he vista trabajar tan rápido a este pueblo.
a2-10.why: Ver has an irregular participle, visto, which never changes for gender; he and the participle always stay together.
